title: The Agni Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa and taught, in the fiction of its frame, by Agni to the sage Vasishtha. It is a compilation, and its chapters draw on older Puranas, law books and technical treatises.
description: The Agni Purana is the most encyclopaedic of the Puranas: in 382 chapters it covers cosmology and the avatars, the duties of kings and the art of war, law and penance, the making of images and the building of temples, ritual and pilgrimage, grammar, prosody, poetics and lexicography, medicine, the marks of gems, and the worship of Vishnu, Shiva and the Goddess.
historicalContext: Written as a summary of the learning a learned householder might need, it is a key witness for the state of many Indian disciplines around the turn of the first millennium and is quoted as such by historians of law, art, medicine and literature.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit text of all 382 chapters as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
